sources.name: Dogwoof
sources.blurb: The premier international documentary specialist: distributing, financing and selling titles like Free Solo and The Cave.

sources.name: Magnolia Pictures
sources.blurb: Major indie distributor behind prominent theatrical docs including RBG, Blackfish and Food, Inc.

sources.name: Kino Lorber
sources.blurb: Art-house distributor with a deep non-fiction catalogue, including Fire at Sea and classic film restorations.

sources.name: NEON
sources.blurb: High-profile theatrical distributor known for prestige, festival-favourite docs such as Flee, All the Beauty and the Bloodshed and Moonage Daydream.

sources.name: Oscilloscope Laboratories
sources.blurb: Independent distributor founded by Adam Yauch, releasing eclectic films like Exit Through the Gift Shop.

sources.name: Greenwich Entertainment
sources.blurb: Boutique company focusing on culture, music and social issues (The Booksellers, Echo in the Canyon).

sources.name: Icarus Films
sources.blurb: Focuses on social, political and historical documentaries from international filmmakers.

sources.name: Sideshow / Janus Films
sources.blurb: Art-house partners handling theatrical releases for major festival docs like EO and All the Beauty and the Bloodshed.

sources.name: First Run Features
sources.blurb: One of America's oldest indie distributors, specialising in human rights, LGBTQ+ and social justice topics.

sources.name: Cinema Guild
sources.blurb: Distributes festival-driven, international and avant-garde non-fiction films.

sources.name: HBO Documentary Films
sources.blurb: Industry giant funding and distributing prestige non-fiction like The Jinx, Going Clear and Welcome to Chechnya.

sources.name: PBS (POV & Independent Lens)
sources.blurb: The primary US public broadcasting home for independent non-fiction filmmaking.

sources.name: CNN Films
sources.blurb: Acquisition and co-production arm behind commercial hits like Navalny, Apollo 11 and Blackfish.

sources.name: ESPN Films / 30 for 30
sources.blurb: Premier producer and distributor of sports and cultural documentaries (O.J.: Made in America).

sources.name: National Geographic Documentary Films
sources.blurb: Focuses on science, nature and high-stakes human endurance (Free Solo, Fire of Love, Sugarcane).

sources.name: BBC Storyville
sources.blurb: The BBC's flagship international documentary strand, commissioning world non-fiction cinema.

sources.name: ARTE
sources.blurb: European public service channel that heavily co-produces and distributes creative documentaries worldwide.

sources.name: Netflix
sources.blurb: Global leader in true crime, feature-length docs and limited series (13th, My Octopus Teacher, The Elephant Whisperers).

sources.name: Apple Original Films
sources.blurb: Focuses on high-budget prestige non-fiction like Boys State and Still: A Michael J. Fox Movie.

sources.name: MUBI
sources.blurb: Curated global platform acquiring festival, foreign and experimental non-fiction.

sources.name: Hulu / Onyx Collective
sources.blurb: Focuses on culture, music and investigative docuseries.

sources.name: Cinephil
sources.blurb: Premier sales agency specialising in international festival docs like Collective and Gunda.

sources.name: Submarine Entertainment
sources.blurb: Major sales agent and production company representing Oscar winners like Summer of Soul and Citizen K.

sources.name: Autlook Filmsales
sources.blurb: Global sales boutique for festival-driven docs like The Painter and the Thief.

sources.name: Deckert Distribution
sources.blurb: Specialises in creative documentaries with a strong focus on Central and Eastern Europe.

releases.title: Don't Let The Bastards Grind You Down
releases.overview: "Don't Let The Bastards Grind You Down" is a documentary film about British social policy. The focus is on the political struggle against neoliberal austerity policies, which have their origins in the hated Thatcher government.  The film features the former socialist MP Dave Nellist, who is now the national chair of the Trade Unionist & Socialist Coalition and Hannah Sell, the general secretary of the Socialist Party. The film features a local election campaign in the miners' town of Nuneaton, students campaigning against an increase in tuition fees and refuse workers from Birmingham striking against massive cuts to their wages.

releases.title: Allies in Exile
releases.overview:
A Storyville documentary that follows Syrian film-makers Hasan Kattan and Fadi Al-Halabi. Having forged a friendship while living through, and filming, the war in Syria, they now face a very different reality as they navigate the UK asylum system.

Turning the camera on themselves, they document a new chapter in their own lives shaped by uncertainty, bureaucracy and displacement, offering a deeply personal and very raw exploration of friendship and belonging. This heart-wrenching film offers an intimate perspective on life in exile and the enduring power of storytelling in the face of adversity.

releases.title: An Unknown Substance
releases.overview: Vladimir Kara-Murza is a prominent Russian opposition politician and Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist who survived two near-fatal poisonings before being sentenced to 25 years in prison after speaking out against Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. This documentary short follows his wife, Evgenia Kara-Murza, during his imprisonment as she mounts a global campaign to bring him home and ensure that his voice would not be silenced.

releases.title: Of Times There Were Before
releases.overview: Of Times There Were Before is a portrait of Romila Thapar, one of the world’s most influential historians and public intellectuals. At ninety-four, having lived through much of the making of modern India, she stands at an unusual distance from the past she has spent a lifetime studying. The film began with a simple question: who is the person behind the historian’s name? Shot at her home in New Delhi, it is an attempt to encounter Thapar beyond the authority of her work and the public image built around it. What emerges is a portrait of a life still in conversation with its own time.

releases.title: This is the House: If I Don’t See You, I Love You
releases.overview: A Ghanaian-American father and daughter duo work through their crowded basement in search of family archives. Through intimate questions and answers, they reconcile the distance caused by immigration, divorce, and loss.

releases.title: Body to Heart
releases.overview: In the picturesque village of Mazan in Southern France, known for the Gisèle Pélicot rape case, three women embark on a journey to heal from domestic and sexual violence by doing horse therapy sessions.

releases.title: Portraits of Slovak and Czech Britain
releases.overview: Transitioning from a photographic exhibition to film, this documentary captures multi-generational stories of Slovak and Czech migrants building lives and finding belonging in Britain. It highlights individuals who have impacted modern British society through personal archives and intimate conversations.

releases.title: Every Grain of Dirt
releases.overview: Every Grain of Dirt documents life in South Lebanon under ongoing threats of displacement and war. As sweeping evacuation orders force over a million people from their homes, some choose to remain. Among them is Ismail, a shepherd who refuses to leave his village — even as bulldozers arrive to erase it, nearly burying him alive as he stands in defiance before the machine.

releases.title: Inside the Mountain
releases.overview: In 1988, Paul Eastwood and his climbing partner became the first men to free-climb Britain's deepest open cave shaft, rising from within the UK's largest underground chamber and traversing around its highest unbroken waterfall, three times the height of Niagara falls. The iconic route will have gone unrepeated for almost 40 years. Decades later a new team of climbers, Olympian Molly Thompson-Smith and legend Steve McClure, will tackle the climb once again, hoping to join the few who have ever free-climbed the route.

releases.title: A Town Called Needville
releases.overview: Told through 35mm photographs and first-person narration, A TOWN CALLED NEEDVILLE traces the filmmaker's four-month inpatient stay at an all-women’s mental health facility in Needville, Texas.

releases.title: My Friend, Kev
releases.overview: A filmmaker reconnects with an old friend, quietly revealing the distance time can create.

releases.title: Journey to the End of the Ego
releases.overview: The scene is the almost mythical landscape of Ben Loyal, one of Scotland's most remote mountains towering over the Arctic Ocean. The cliff is one of the finest sweeps of clean unclimbed rock to be found anywhere in the land. The climber is the thought-provoking controversial live-wire, who goes by the name of Franco Cookson. This is the epic story of the UK's most dangerous trad route and the 105 days of climbing it took to realise one man's dream; 'Nothing is Lost' E12 7a.

releases.title: The Emerald Underground
releases.overview: A short documentary following the stories of three independent bands from across Ireland; The Psychs, IMLÉ and Dead Assets. Each band shares their passion for music, the many struggles they face on their journey, and what keeps them going.

releases.title: Life Sure Is Sweet
releases.overview: Two years in the making, "Life Sure Is Sweet" is a independent coming-of-age snowboard documentary produced by the creative collective TDI (Technically Doing It). Featuring an all-Black and Brown crew of riders travelling and filming across the globe, the film moves beyond high-level action sports progression to explore deep themes of cultural identity, community, lifelong friendship, and charting your own path in the mountains.

releases.title: Beyond
releases.overview: Follows people living with and beyond cancer as they discover strength, connection, and a new sense of possibility through climbing. Set between indoor walls and wild mountain rock, it is a powerful story about recovery becoming adventure.

releases.title: Musk
releases.overview: An incisive look behind the legend of Elon Musk, the world’s most heralded 'inventor-entrepreneur' who has enormous influence on the world in which we all live.

releases.title: George Michael: The Faith Tour
releases.overview: A stunning delve into George Michael's 1988 Faith Tour, as shot live at the famous Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy. This exclusive footage, assembled from a 14-camera shoot captured on 35mm over two nights (30–31 May 1988), features the 24-year-old pop star at the height of his powers.

releases.title: Avedon
releases.overview: Richard Avedon’s photographs didn’t just reflect culture, they shaped it, and continue to do so. The feature documentary AVEDON traces the life and legacy of an artist who used fashion, portraiture, and commercial photography to explore identity, power, fear and beauty. With unprecedented access to Avedon’s archive, including never before seen photos, behind the scenes recordings, and interviews with those who knew him best, AVEDON is a visually stunning examination of the mind of an artist who shaped our collective image of the 20th century.

releases.title: Making Marie Antoinette
releases.overview: Eleanor Coppola turns her camera on her daughter, Sofia, as she shoots Marie Antoinette. Catching every detail of the behind-the-scenes and on-set action, Eleanor captures the feat of Sofia’s directing a landmark film aged 34, and muses on what it means for a mother to watch her daughter at work.

releases.title: Finding Faith
releases.overview: A short film contextualising the cultural significance of George Michael's Faith Tour via unheard interview voice-over, unseen images by Herb Ritts, and behind-the-scenes footage of the Faith music video.

otherDates.note: Precedes screenings of George Michael: The Faith Tour

releases.title: Manhood
releases.overview:
Dallas businessman Bill Moore aims to make penis enlargement as commonplace as Botox and bring the procedure into the mainstream, positioning male cosmetic surgery as a growing part of the aesthetics industry.

The documentary follows several men, including an OnlyFans creator and a father of five, as they put their bodies on the line and undergo surgery in pursuit of physical transformation.

Through intimate access to both the practitioners selling the dream and the men buying into it, the film traces the insecurities, trauma and societal pressures driving each of them, while raising uncomfortable questions about the ethics of an industry built on male self-doubt.

Filmed over two years, with dark humour and unexpected tenderness, this is a timely and revealing portrait of identity and self-image as cosmetic surgery among men continues to rise.

releases.title: Magic in the Mundane
releases.overview: A cinematic journey into the overlooked miracles of everyday existence.

releases.title: Whispers in the Woods
releases.overview: In the heart of the tranquil Vosges forests, where lynxes, bears and deer roam freely, Vincent Munier accompanies his father on his expeditions. He not only seeks to capture the visual wonders of this forest kingdom, but also aims to make its sounds audible. Every whisper of the forest is a reminder of the knowledge of nature that his father once imbued in him – knowledge that Vincent now passes on to his own son. Vincent Munier combines breathtaking footage of nature and its sounds to create a fairytale-like cinematic experience that slows time down.

releases.title: Nuisance Bear
releases.overview: A polar bear is forced to navigate a human world of tourists, wildlife officers, and hunters as its ancient migration collides with modern life. When a sacred predator is branded a nuisance, it becomes unclear who truly belongs in this shared landscape.

releases.title: Whiddy
releases.overview: A small rural community in Ireland welcomes in a major, global oil company with open arms but just 10 years and numerous oil spills later, that dream turns into an unimaginable nightmare. 50 lives lost in a tragedy that silenced and divided the community and still haunts it to this day.

releases.title: 1 in 2
releases.overview: Nearly one in two of us will be diagnosed with cancer at some point in our lives. David Nicholas Wilkinson is one of them, twice over. 1 in 2 follows Wilkinson through his own treatment, where he discovers a steep rise in bowel cancer among people far too young to be screened for it, and far too young, it seems, to be believed.

releases.title: A Fox Under a Pink Moon
releases.overview: At just 16, Soraya is already creating stunning drawings and sculptures that are as beautiful as they are dark. This strong-willed Afghan sculptor and illustrator has been trying for five years to escape Iran and join her mother in Austria.

releases.title: Women and War
releases.overview: In a chalet in the Ukrainian mountains, four women attend therapy sessions to recover from their very different, deeply traumatic experiences of the war. They each try, in their own way, to resume their former lives.

releases.title: The Neighbourhood is Changing
releases.overview: Documentary on the making and legacy of Mulberry Street featuring new interviews with cast and crew

releases.title: When a Witness Recants
releases.overview: In 1983, author Ta-Nehisi Coates learned that a 14-year-old boy was murdered in his Baltimore middle school. Upon revisiting the case, he uncovers the truth: Three innocent teenagers were wrongfully convicted and spent 36 years in prison — creating a lasting impact on the accused, the witnesses, and their community.

releases.title: Good Luck, Kid
releases.overview: Grit, gear, growth – this film is a portrait of Taylor Shaffer’s coming-of-age as a photographer and filmmaker, following his creative trajectory as he shepherds Alex Honnold and Tommy Caldwell through a 2,500-mile expedition to attempt a single-day traverse of the Devil’s Thumb massif and finds his artistic voice amid risk, friendship, and a changing Alaskan landscape.

releases.title: Observer
releases.overview: Filmmaker Ian Cheney embarks on an experiment in which he brings a series of keen-eyed observers - scientists, artists, a hunter - to a range of locations around the world, often without telling them where they are going, and asks them simply to describe what they see. What unfolds is a deep exploration and celebration of the power of observation: what happens when you find new ways to sense and perceive the world around you?

releases.title: Robson
releases.overview: Two of the world’s most accomplished ski mountaineers, Christina Lustenberger and Guillaume Pierrel, have carved their names into history with bold first descents across the globe. Now, turning their sights on Mount Robson, the highest and most formidable peak in the Canadian Rockies, they retrace the steps of pioneering alpinists who came before them, pushing the line between past and present. Battling towering walls of ice, snow and rock, unpredictable weather, and the weight of a dream that has challenged generations, their journey becomes as much about resilience and legacy as it is about the pursuit of a descent few have ever dared to imagine.

releases.title: My Grandmother’s Sketchbook: Under Mont Blanc
releases.overview: A 30-year-old sketchbook leads Max Romey to the Mont Blanc region. The Alaska-based watercolor artist and environmental advocate sets out to follow in the footsteps of his grandmother, who visited this landscape in the late 1990s and captured it in dozens of drawings. With mountain guide Hillary Gerardi, Max attempts to locate each sketch’s exact origin point. Many match perfectly—until the Mer de Glace throws him off course. The glacier has changed too much in 30 years to recognize.

releases.title: The Himalayas in My Heart
releases.overview: In 1802, the Survey of India Institute launched the Great Trigonometrical Survey, a colossal undertaking aimed at precisely mapping British India from which the world became aware of the vast scale of the Himalayan range. From August to November 2024, using these historical maps, Jérémy Bigé makes his way on foot over 2,300km from Indian Kashmir to central Nepal. His goal: to connect the various Himalayan cultures in a single journey by following routes from the past.

releases.title: À bord du vide
releases.overview: A poetic exploration of the art of steep skiing with Aurélien Lardy. This film celebrates the art of the movement, the commitment, and the intimate relationship between the man and the mountain, and what draws us to vertical places.

releases.title: Back By Tea Time
releases.overview: In a world where it feels like we have everything we could ever want at our fingertips – Amazon, Spotify, next-day delivery, door-to-door, Uber, Netflix, Deliveroo, quicker than ever before, pure convenience and luxury without a second thought – in that world, perhaps there is something to be said for choosing the long way round. When Alice Lemkes realises she's out of milk, it is an excuse for an adventure in ‘Scotland's Last Great Wilderness.’

releases.title: It Takes Two To Tandem
releases.overview: Longtime riding partners Sam and Jazz take a tandem bike across some of their favourite trails in the Rockies, marking ten years since their first tandem adventure together. Part celebration, part reflection, the film explores friendship, trust, and the rare joy of moving through the world in sync.

releases.title: Nininbaori
releases.overview: Follows three para-climbers through fragments of their daily lives, where ordinary domestic gestures intertwine with the quiet precision of athletic practice. Moving seamlessly from one to the next, the film refuses hierarchy, unfolding instead like the pages of a single book written by multiple hands.

releases.title: My Ride or Die
releases.overview: Morgan McGlashon (professional mountain guide) and Caite Zeliff (professional skier) picked obscure paths. Those paths collided and became intertwined. When their careers took off they found themselves spending less time in the mountains together but they always dreamed of one day coming back together on a proper adventure. On a 10-day expedition in Alaska, the two reconnect.

releases.title: More than Everest: The Life of T.H. Somervell
releases.overview: T. Howard Somervell (1890-1975) is best known for his role in the 1922 and 1924 expeditions to climb Everest. This film explores the lesser known aspects of Somervell's remarkable life as a missionary surgeon, artist and composer of music.

releases.title: Kidical Mass
releases.overview: After years of exploring their world by bicycle, the Moss family knew that they wanted to raise their kids on two wheels. But after a frightening accident on the way to school, they had to take a step back from their pedal-powered ambitions. Then they found Kidical Mass. This is the story of how one family is helping to reclaim their streets, one giant kid bike party at a time.

releases.title: The Search for Milliseconds
releases.overview: Inside mountain bike downhill phenom Jackson Goldstone's high-stakes bid to become one of the youngest riders in history to claim the UCI DH Elite overall title. From pre-season testing to the tense, pressure-filled moments leading into the last race of the year, the film follows Jackson and the team that supports him as they hunt for every possible edge in a sport where the smallest fractions of time can define a champion. With the title on the line and only one decisive run remaining, Jackson prepares to risk everything for the win.

releases.title: You Can See Everything
releases.overview: Thirty-four days before she's sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

releases.title: Everest: The Other Side
releases.overview: An intimate portrait of two people bound by love, ambition, and the pursuit of the impossible. Elite ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson fell deeply in love while reaching the pinnacle of their sport. Their drive sharpened into a shared dream: to climb and ski the direct North Face of Mount Everest—the most difficult and dangerous climb on the mountain and the most coveted ski line on Earth—something only a handful have ever achieved, and no one has successfully skied down.

releases.title: American Doctor
releases.overview: United by a shared oath to save lives, three American doctors—Palestinian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian—work in a besieged hospital in Gaza in the middle of a genocide comitted by Israel, and return to the United States to fight for the patients and colleagues they left behind.

releases.title: Obsession: The Beryl Burton Story
releases.overview: A documentary about Britain’s greatest athlete. Undefeated for 25 years, Leeds-born amateur cyclist Beryl Burton won seven World Championships, beat men’s records and transformed women’s sport; all while working on a Yorkshire rhubarb farm. Through unseen archive, letters and intimate interviews, the film explores the glory of her achievements and the cost of her obsession, particularly on her relationship with her daughter Denise, who followed her into competitive cycling.

releases.title: Bloomin' Octopus!
releases.overview: Explores the sudden rise in octopus numbers in south west England through a series of interconnected perspectives, showing how shifts beneath the surface ripple outward, affecting ecosystems and people alike.

releases.title: SILA
releases.overview: Set on an island 600 kilometers north of the Arctic Circle, this intimate vérité portrait follows two young Inuit coming of age. Created in close collaboration with a local children’s home and filmed in the Greenlandic language, the story traces identity, tradition, loss, and resilience. Living alongside its protagonists, the film observes a fragile passage between deep cultural roots and an uncertain, rapidly changing world.

releases.title: Same Sun - Cycling through Africa
releases.originalTitle: Same Sun - Mit dem Fahrrad durch Afrika
releases.overview: The story of Wiebke Lühmann's journey from Freiburg to the Cape of Good Hope. Honest, raw, and close to the inner and outer challenges of a 430-day bicycle trip. Her journey takes her through 22 countries, Sahara storms, the rain season, the Congo Basin, and the deserts of Namibia. What begins as a search for independence becomes an intimate exploration of identity.

releases.title: Big Jim: An American on Everest
releases.overview: “Big Jim” Whittaker (1929-2026) was a legendary Pacific Northwest mountaineer who became the first American to summit Mount Everest on May 1, 1963. This short documentary explores his “brotherhood of the rope” with his twin brother, Lou, as well as Nawang Gombu Sherpa, his Everest climbing partner and lifelong friend. Featuring rarely seen 16mm footage from the 1963 Everest Expedition, archival images from the Whittaker family collection, and interviews filmed in Jim’s late 80s, the film is both an intimate portrait of an extraordinary life and a celebration of the adventurous spirit that helped define a generation of climbers.

releases.title: The Hillbilly Scientist
releases.overview: While modern running has evolved toward sleek curation, optimisation, and commercialisation, Lazarus Lake has spent 50 years designing formats with an unapologetic, honest difficulty. The Hillbilly Scientist reveals that Laz’s cruellest courses are rooted in a deeply scientific understanding of human psychology and physical limits. This is the only official documentary dedicated to the creator of the Barkley Marathons and Big’s Backyard Ultra. Filmed over more than a year, it reveals the man behind the myth through never-before-seen footage, exclusive testimonials, and exceptional access to Laz’s world.

releases.title: Borrowed from the Earth
releases.overview: Tells the story of the powerful connection between the Blackfeet people and horses, and how that life-giving relationship remains alive today. Throughout their histories, both horse and Indigenous people have been corralled - horses by fences, and Indigenous people onto reservations. Yet centuries-long attempts to subdue both ultimately strengthened the bond between them. Saddle up for a visually poetic journey from the origin story of the horse to the modern day Indian Relay Race. Filmed on the Blackfeet Reservation in Browning, Montana.

releases.title: Glacier's Requiem
releases.overview: In isolation on Iceland’s Snæfellsnes Peninsula, Nigerian-born modular synthesis artist Colloboh transforms glacial and oceanic recordings into sonic compositions; uncovering a dialogue between ice and sea that reshapes his understanding of consciousness, ecological collapse, and humanity’s place within both.

releases.title: 75 Seconds
releases.overview: On a foggy March evening in Norway, freeskier Jacob Wester triggers an avalanche and is swept off a cliff. For 75 seconds, he fights for his life inside a roaring mass of snow, while his wife Sofia waits in silence below. This is an account of chaos, fear, and hope inside an avalanche.

releases.title: Dreamrime
releases.overview: Sit back and marvel at this cinematic wonder as we see the famous Cerro Torre towers of Patagonia like never before. Filmed by local drone expert Ty Lekki and produced by multi-award winner Alastair Lee, this film is a glorious marriage of sound and vision as we enter a new phase of mountain film making. A team of three Argentinian and one German Alpinists attempt the Punta Hernon/Torre Egger traverse, encountering the unique rime and mushroom formations found only in this special part of the world.

releases.title: Blank Patterns
releases.overview: A collection of athlete portraits following Jacob Bélanger, Emma Patterson, and Ugo Troubat. Through their individual stories, the film explores the experiences, choices, and communities that shaped the lives they lead today. While each has taken a different path, together they reflect the many ways people find their place within skiing and contribute to the culture in their own way.

releases.title: Bas Van Steenbergen - Interlude
releases.overview: Bas Van Steenbergen heads up Mt. Seymour on Vancouver's North Shore — the birthplace of freeride —riding with a rhythm all his own.

releases.title: Aldo's Raptor Roundup
releases.overview: Six-year old Aldo spends an exciting weekend banding migrating raptors in Cape May, New Jersey with his friend John, a volunteer bander with the Cape May Raptor Banding Project.

releases.title: Phantom 814
releases.overview: Heavy Weekend 03: Unique access to the most mysterious organisation in France. Jake Hanrahan travels with the bizarre syndicate known as "814SSR". They shoot guns, host fight clubs, and make money in the underground. Yet still, they insist they're not a gang and are simply doing hardcore trolling. The truth? Decide for yourself...

releases.title: A Mystical Ornithology
releases.overview: Immersed in the songs of blue jays, yellow-throated warblers, and red-shouldered hawks on his forty-six-acre farm in rural South Carolina, acclaimed poet and ornithologist J. Drew Lanham exchanges calls with the birds that stop over at his home during their seasonal migrations. For Drew, these creatures are gods, transcendent beings who summon a response of reverence. Reverberating with sound, music, light, and ethereal cinematic expression, A Mystical Ornithology weaves a kinetic texture for the senses and invites you into a poetic evocation of the paradox of love and grief within the changing nature of the seasons.

releases.title: Planet Health Stories - Breathe Her In
releases.overview: For the women and non-binary runners of 10Ironwomen - a collective addressing the gender imbalance in endurance sports - Bristol's green trails offer what city streets can't: space to breathe.

releases.title: Find Mòr
releases.overview: Scotland still has its mysteries roaring in remote glens and sometimes hidden in plain sight. Find Mòr follows a group of canyoneers over the span of two years as they embark on a journey of exploration into the hidden corners of the Scottish Highlands. The film offers a unique perspective from within the relatively unknown niche community and discovers the myriad motivations that drive this passion of curiosity. Setting out in search of uncharted canyons, they find true adventure and forge deep connections to people and place.

releases.title: The Last of the Lookouts
releases.overview: High atop Sinkut Mountain in northern British Columbia, Bart Vanderlinde begins each summer's day the way he has for the past nine years: scanning the forest for smoke. He's among the last lookout people in the province. Where three hundred lookouts once formed an interconnected network across the region, Bart now often keeps watch alone. This is an intimate portrait of a man and a profession facing obsolescence. The film gives insight into the craft of fire detection while capturing the quiet solitude of a life lived in observation.

releases.title: Building Apollo 13
releases.overview: What begins as a challenge on the rock becomes a profound process of dedication and commitment. Caro North, Fay Manners, Rocio Rodriguez Guiñazú and Belén Prados devote their time, bodies, and hearts to opening a new route in a remote place, Turbio IV in Patagonia, Argentina, building not only a challenge but also a way of inhabiting and sharing the mountain. What makes it unique is their willingness to dedicate the necessary time and care to leave the route immaculate and safe for other climbers to enjoy; not simply to climb a wall, but to create something that can be shared with others.

releases.title: The Kelp Collector
releases.overview: After a career in science, Sandy Webb has found a new passion in retirement: collecting and cataloguing the diverse algae species that inhabit the waters near her Melbourne home. With the precision of a scientist and the eye of an artist, she transforms her discoveries into exquisite pressed-seaweed specimens, The kelp collector reveals how Sandy's dedication to documenting local marine life connects her to the coastal environment she calls home.

releases.title: Rongo
releases.overview: With plenty of powder to go around, un-ridden waves rolling into secret golden beaches, and local characters to greet you with a smile, six professional athletes make the most of every moment during an action-packed adventure through Aotearoa, NZ!

releases.title: Forward
releases.overview: Celebrate the power of adaptive adventure through the inspiring journey of Clay March — a young man with cerebral palsy whose passion for skiing, surfing, and exploring the outdoors knows no bounds. Set against the awe-inspiring landscapes of British Columbia, Clay, his triplet brother Tanner, and a vibrant cast of renowned adaptive athletes set out to defy expectations and redefine what inclusion in the outdoors truly means.

releases.title: Against the Clock
releases.overview: A short documentary exploring the life and passion of cyclist Alasdair Washington. Blending race footage with moments of personal reflection, the film offers an honest portrait of his lasting connection to the sport. It looks at the discipline, determination and enjoyment that continue to fuel his competitive spirit. Rather than focusing on results alone, the story captures the essence of what it means to keep showing up and pushing forward. What keeps the wheels turning when time refuses to slow down? Both intimate and authentic, the film celebrates a lifelong passion for cycling and community.

releases.title: Elsewhere: Randi Skaug
releases.overview: Randi Skaug was the first Norwegian woman to climb Mount Everest and went on to complete the Seven Summits. She has led expeditions around the world, written books and inspired thousands of people to embrace the outdoors. Now going through cancer treatment and unable to return to her remote island house, Randi welcomes us into her eclectic home in Oslo. As her world grows smaller, her perspective grows clearer. For Randi, a lifetime of extraordinary achievement has led to one simple conclusion: be kind.

releases.title: Beura
releases.overview: The tale of the Cailleach Bheur, the Celtic goddess of nature, storms and winter, is well known to many in the Gàidhealtachd. Said to have carved the mountains and glens with ice, and borne the islands like children on her back, the Cailleach disappeared long ago leaving us only with her song – a sad, cautionary tale. This Gaelic arts project brings music, film and verse together to reimagine Cailleach’s story for the modern era.

releases.title: Casey
releases.overview: Casey is a young woman on a journey of self-empowerment, shaped by community and a fierce love for skateboarding. This short film is a tribute to trans+ joy and the spaces that allow people to be unapologetically themselves. Made in collaboration with Transkaters and Not A Phase charity.

releases.title: Framed
releases.overview: Siebe Vanhee sets out to onsight Voie Petit, a brutal 12-pitch 8a+ line at 3,500m on the Grand Capucin, completely alone - no partner, no static ropes, just lead rope-solo technique and a drone circling above. But even a solo mission as a professional climber has a crew: a manager on the phone, a sponsor waiting for footage, a director on the glacier, and Vanhee himself playing climber, cameraman and storyteller all at once, selfie-interviewing his own exhaustion pitch by pitch.

releases.title: Hotpipe Hillbillies
releases.overview: A documentary about community, resilience, and finding joy in the most unlikely of places. Against the backdrop of Shoreham’s industrial shoreline, a diverse crew of surfers gather at an industrial outflow pipe to ride waves that are often messy, fickle, and short-lived. This ain’t Cornwall. It sure ain’t California. But for this crew, it’s home

releases.title: Ripple
releases.overview: Two women sit by the lake that raised them and have a conversation about what it means to be a freeride skier. After dedicating their lives to the sport, they question the meaning of it all. More than anything, this is a story about surrendering to the present moment. A story about being water.

releases.title: The Anti Expedition
releases.overview: Bob, a young professor of outdoor education, was searching for an ethos to guide his teaching when he stumbled upon a film made in 1971. The film depicted three mountaineers who chose not to summit a Himalayan mountain out of respect for local beliefs. For Bob, it was this film, and the work of Sigmund Kvaløy (one of the three mountaineers), that spurred a lifelong passion for ‘place responsive’ outdoor adventure. In The Anti Expedition, Bob and a team of seasoned adventure guides return the 1971 film to the Sherpa community of the Rolwaling Valley. In a fascinating look at how five decades has affected both the valley and its people, they rediscover that it's not the destination that makes the journey meaningful.

releases.title: Folk Who Roam
releases.overview: Sheffield-based violin maker Emma Hardy is bridging the gap between nature and music by designing and hand-crafting a uniquely decorated violin inspired by the Peak District’s history of folk music and land access rights.

releases.title: The Art of Hold Shaping
releases.overview: An intimate documentary exploring the world of Dan Yagmin as the creative force behind Decoy Holds. Moving between wild landscapes, workshop processes and climbing walls, the film is a portrait of an artist shaping not just holds, but the way we experience climbing itself.

releases.title: I Follow Rivers
releases.overview: Mariann Sæther is one of the best whitewater kayakers in the world. Since she was a teenager, she has challenged expectations within sport and society. When she becomes a mother, she is determined she can both be an extreme sports athlete and have a family. But is life on the river really worth the risk?

releases.title: It's What You Make It
releases.overview: Lars has figured out what he loves - snowboarding. This film explores his approach to surfstyle carving and what keeps him coming back after 35 years. For him, carving becomes a form of expression, feeling and freedom.

releases.title: CeCe's Way
releases.overview: As a young woman with additional needs, CeCe understands how it can feel to find things difficult, and she brings that compassion and understanding to her role as a ride leader with the New Forest Off Road Club.

releases.title: 3 Peaks Cyclocross
releases.overview: First run in 1961 by the Bradford Cycling Club, the classic race crosses Pen-y-Ghent, Whernside and Ingleborough, three fells above the River Ribble in the Yorkshire Dales. The course is now 61km in length, with 33km on unsurfaced ground, 28km on road, and six to eight km that the organisers deem unrideable. Join Lachlan Morton for a cyclocross race like no other.

releases.title: The Oldest Munro Bagger
releases.overview: Filmed over four years, the film follows 80 year-old Nick Gardner as he attempts to complete all 282 of Scotland's Munros in the wake of his beloved wife's dementia diagnosis. A moving, authentic story of enduring love and growth, told against the breathtaking backdrop of the Scottish Highlands.

releases.title: Chuey
releases.overview: Since moving from Malaysia to London in the 1970s, Malaysian-Chinese Buddhist and therapist Chuey has transformed the garden of her family home into a sanctuary of global flora; blending plants from across continents, her garden and personal story entwine in quiet narratives of migration, memory, and finding belonging. Set in the suburbs of North-West London as summer winds down, this meditative short invites us into her intimate reflections, offering a story of resilience, unity, and nature's power to dissolve barriers.

releases.title: Roots
releases.overview: More than 200 days of the year, you can find local Vermonter and ski patroller Ethan Parrish skiing some of the most extreme terrain in the Vermont backcountry. Ethan is aware of the impact of outsiders on local life, from the strain on community to reckless practices in the backcountry. While clearing the land surrounding his great-uncle’s farmhouse, he dreams of his own future, living off the land and skiing Vermont’s Green Mountains. Roots explores his deep connection to the mountains, the people in his life, and his home.

releases.title: The Long Way Home
releases.overview: Kelly Halpin has long dreamed of completing a full traverse of the beautiful and seldom travelled Gros Ventre mountain range right in her backyard in Wyoming. The route is 50 miles off-trail over technical terrain and hits every major summit in the range. After years of scouting and two failed attempts the film shows the power of perseverance and dreaming big while staying close to home.

releases.title: Marcus & Me
releases.overview: As a participant in the Outdoor Inclusion Coalition, 'little' Marcus explores the less-known corners of his Pittsburgh back yard to seek out opportunities for climbing and connection with nature.

releases.title: Not Just Running
releases.overview: An intimate portrait of an athlete who finds in movement a way to understand herself, grow, and continue shaping her own path. Through her preparation, training sessions, and the quiet moments that come before competition, the film approaches Joyce Njeru not only as an elite runner, but as a person shaped by her culture, determination, discipline, and a deep connection with the terrain.

releases.title: Rodeo On Ice
releases.overview: With skijoring poised to become a potential addition to the 2030 Winter Olympics, lifelong equestrian Britta Nancarrow assembles a team to push her skijoring to the next level. The film follows Nancarrow as she trains with skier Mike King and snowboarder Sandra Hillen, taking their on-snow skills to their very first competition.

releases.title: Ridgeline
releases.overview: Professional musician and composer Liz Derstine heads into the wilderness to chase a very different goal: attempting a self-supported Fastest Known Time on the Pacific Crest Trail.

releases.title: Searching for SuperCrust: The Lost Tapes
releases.overview: Five cyclists set out to cross Europe's largest glacier by bike. An expedition 30 years in the making, the film explores the past, present, and future of Vatnajökull through the stories of those who have braved the glacier’s icy expanse on two wheels.

releases.title: Sam Hodgson - The Story of a Freerider
releases.overview: There was never a plan B. Not out of stubbornness, but because Sam Hodgson never needed one. Growing up on a farm, somewhere between dirt, shovels and bikes, it was clear early on: if there’s nothing to ride, you build it yourself.

releases.title: Remember the Summit
releases.overview: Sir Chris Bonington’s return to Torres del Paine, 62 years after the first ascent of the Central Tower.  At 91 years old, and while living with Alzheimer’s disease, the documentary accompanies Bonington in a profoundly human return: an attempt to reconnect with memories that time has erased, but that the Patagonian landscape still seems to guard. During the filming, Chris once again set foot on the territory of Estancia Cerro Guido, closing a circle between past and present, between the epic of mountaineering and the fragility of memory.

releases.title: The Lost Cache
releases.overview: History, science and exploration converged in a quest to find the lost camera of one of climbing’s most iconic photographers and cartographers, Bradford Washburn. Set against the backdrop of the pioneering lensmen’s storied 1937 Mount Lucania expedition, this film blurs the lines between adventure documentary, treasure hunt and meditation on why we risk everything to chase the improbable.

releases.title: Chasing Sub 2
releases.overview: A shared dream. A common belief.  Chasing Sub 2 is the journey towards realizing the impossible: running the world's first sub-two-hour marathon. A decade-long pursuit sparked by Haile Gebrselassie at the 2008 Berlin Marathon, which became a reality at the 2026 London Marathon.  Kenyan marathoner, Sabastian Sawe, has won all four of the marathons he has competed in. Adding to his extensive list of accolades is the historic 1:59:30 finish, powered by the latest Adizero innovation: the Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3. The fastest and lightest Adizero super-shoe ever made, weighing less than 100 grams.  Humanity just got faster.

releases.title: The Impossible Journey
releases.overview: In 2013 Danish adventurer, Thor Pedersen, left his loved ones behind and set off in an attempt to become the first person to visit every country in the world without flying. He wanted adventure, a title, and to show that the world is a much better place than is portrayed in the news. He got an experience that tested every layer of him as a human being.

releases.title: Black Eyes
releases.overview: In Mongolia's timeless Altai Mountains, 13-year-old Kharakoz embodies a captivating blend of ancestral traditions and modern influences. As she learns the ancient art of eagle-hunting, the film delves into the powerful ripple effect of passing this sacred knowledge to girls.

releases.title: Excalibur, A Pursuit in Process
releases.overview: Brooke Raboutou takes on Excalibur (5.15c / 9b+) in Arco, Italy. This film documents the process, hardships, and relentless perseverance—both mental and physical—behind her pursuit of one of the hardest routes in the world. At just 18 moves, Excalibur is a brutally condensed testpiece of pure power endurance on razor-sharp holds. Brooke’s ascent not only marks a leap in her career – becoming the first woman to climb 5.15c / 9b+ – but also represents a meaningful step in closing the long-standing gap between men and women at the absolute cutting edge of sport climbing.

releases.title: Small People, Big Adventures - Currents of Curiosity
releases.overview: Renowned explorer Leo Houlding embarks on a remarkable family expedition to the Calvados Island chain - one of the most remote inhabited regions on Earth, located 300km off the coast of Papua New Guinea. Here, money is meaningless and life is sustained through subsistence living, deep connection to nature and community exchange.

releases.title: The Dawn Wall By Your Side
releases.overview: The Dawn Wall is the hardest big wall in the world. After his failure in 2021, Seb Berthe sets sail again for a second attempt. Strongly supported by Soline Kentzel, Seb will have to give his all to, maybe, achieve his lifetime dream. But he is not the only one with a dream, and Soline also embarks on an extremely ambitious ascent. More than a story of performance, this documentary intimately and deeply questions, through Soline’s perspective, the meaning of the climbing partnership.

releases.title: Skyclimber: Scaling the Eiffel Tower
releases.overview: A climber attempts to scale the Eiffel Tower in a documentary that is equal parts high-altitude adventure and intimate personal portrait.

releases.title: Hunter's Moon
releases.overview: Ski mountaineers Christina ‘Lusti’ Lustenberger and Guillaume ‘Gee’ Pierrel carve a first ski descent on New Zealand's Aoraki / Mt. Cook.

releases.title: Alaska
releases.overview: Join us for glacier camping and skiing big lines in remote Alaska.

releases.title: All Rivers Spill Their Stories to the Sea
releases.overview: On England’s North East coast, where rivers, heavy industry and the sea have shaped lives for generations, fisherman Stan Rennie is watching the world he knows disappear. His family have worked these waters for generations. Then, almost overnight, thousands of dead crabs and lobsters wash ashore, and a community already living with uncertainty is pushed into crisis. Teesside filmmaker Jeanie Finlay brings warmth, wit and deep local feeling to this David-and-Goliath story of environmental damage, official evasions and working-class resilience. At its centre is Stan: funny, stubborn, vulnerable and increasingly determined to be heard.

releases.title: Amazomania
releases.overview: In 1996, a Brazilian official and a Swedish journalist ventured into the Amazon to document the isolated Korubo tribe caught in escalating land conflicts. Initially hailed as a heroic breakthrough, the footage now demands to be reexamined. Uncovering the hidden costs of “discovery,” the film confronts the colonial legacy and exposes the long-term repercussions for the Korubo.

releases.title: No Trees, No Seas
releases.overview: A people-led climate documentary rooted in Cornwall, where stories, science and surfing come together to reveal how restoring the connections between land, sea and community could change everything.

releases.title: E11
releases.overview: Multi-award winning E11 tells the story behind the first ascent of Rhapsody, a route considered to be the hardest traditional rock climb in the world. Told in an offbeat dramadoc style the film attempts to understand what it takes to climb a route of this standard and strives to get inside the head of its first ascentionist, the understated yet quite remarkable Dave MacLeod.

releases.title: NIO KO BOKK (This Belongs to All of Us)
releases.overview: Pape and Seydi are two young men who find purpose and community in the ocean, choosing a different path than the perilous journeys many peers take in search of opportunity abroad. Through their story, the film explores how belonging at home can be as powerful as the promise of elsewhere.

releases.title: Escape the Indoors: A 5pm-9am Cargo Bike Adventure
releases.overview: School's out and the cargo bike is loaded. One night, one tent, one bag of marshmallows. World-class cyclist Tracy Moseley and family swap four walls for moonlight, time outside, s'mores by the campfire and a spot of rain.

releases.title: Running High
releases.overview: Dutch ultrarunner Noor van der Veen sets out to achieve a Fastest Known Time (FKT) on the Pyrenean Haute Route.

releases.title: Kirsten Van Horne - Rising Tide
releases.overview: From a shy, small-town kid to competing on the biggest stage in freeride mountain biking, Kristen’s journey shows what can happen when you give yourself permission to try.

releases.title: Oly's Dean
releases.overview: Set along British Columbia’s remote Dean River, the film follows 9-year-old Oly Hickman as he moves through his family’s fishing lodge in the heart of steelhead country.

releases.title: Old Ladies Against Underwater Garbage
releases.overview: Follow Susan Baur, the 85-year-old leader, and her crew of fearless women as they defy limits, protect the environment, and rediscover wonder and joy through water and community.

releases.title: Rob Lowe: The Outsider
releases.overview: Traces Lowe's career from his breakout roles in “The Outsiders” and “St. Elmo’s Fire” to his Emmy-nominated performance on “The West Wing” and how he maintained his Hollywood career.

releases.title: SO ALIVE!
releases.overview: A fictional boy aims to become a non-fictional rapper. His label has other plans.

releases.title: To Hold a Mountain
releases.overview: In the remote highlands of Montenegro, a shepherd mother and daughter proudly defend their ancestral mountain from the threat of becoming a NATO military training ground, stirring memories of the violence that shattered their family.

releases.title: 14th
releases.overview: Revolves around the equal protection and citizenship-focused 14th amendment, which was ratified in 1868 in the turbulent era of Reconstruction and has been a contentious part of the American body politic ever since.

releases.title: Who Is Still Alive
releases.overview: A map of Gaza, its towns, camps and neighbourhoods. White paint on a black ground. Within the crudely drawn outlines, nine refugees who escaped the inferno tell their stories.

releases.title: Maverick: The Epic Adventures of David Lean
releases.overview: Profiles the double Oscar winner, who helmed some of the most well-respected movies of all time, via never-before-seen archive and contributions from leading film directors. Haunted by the shadow of his dismissive father and his puritan upbringing, Lean was married six times, and he created layered and complex narratives in his work while struggling to find connection and meaning in his personal life.

releases.title: Slava: Shooting with Music
releases.overview: Sviatoslav Vakarchuk is the lead singer of Okean Elzy, Ukraine's most successful rock band. He is a former politician and activist who has a PhD in theoretical physics. Slava has been compared to Bruce Springsteen and Paul McCartney and his songs are an important part of Ukrainian identity, part of the country's cultural DNA. He is now channeling his talents to liberate his country.

releases.title: Back to the Beginning: Ozzy's Final Bow
releases.overview: A powerful return to roots, this concert captures Black Sabbath in peak form - reuniting to deliver classic hits with raw energy and legendary precision.

releases.title: Tutu
releases.overview: Through never-before-seen archival footage and first-hand accounts of those who knew him best, the film traces Archbishop Desmond Tutu’s rise as the voice of the oppressed, guided by faith, hope and an understanding of the power of forgiveness.

releases.title: Rehearsals for a Revolution
releases.overview: Through five portraits of relatives and mentors, five expressions of resistance, Pegah Ahangarani sketches her life story. Drawing from personal archives, home videos, street protests footage, newspapers, and recorded voices, she retraces more than 40 years of Iran’s history. From the early days of 1979, until the war that began in 2026, she pieces together intimate and collective memories, forming the portrait of a country shaped by political repression and in constant hope for a revolution.

otherDates.note: New York City and Los Angeles

releases.title: Each Day in a Moment: 2026
releases.overview: One person’s perspective of the year 2026 shown through an accumulation of 365 unedited shots.

releases.title: Renoir & Love
releases.overview: Pierre-Auguste Renoir is one of the world’s favourite artists, a founding member of the Impressionist movement and a constantly evolving artist. With exclusive access to the National Gallery’s new exciting show of the same name (3 October 2026 – 31 January 2027), Exhibition on Screen will bring Renoir’s world class works to cinema audiences. Be transported back to a Parisian summer of love through the eyes of a true visionary. An unmissable opportunity to fall in love with Renoir this winter.
